title: `is_queued_for_deletion()` still returns `true` after `cancel_free()` is called
body:
### Tested versions

v4.4.1.stable.official [49a5bc7b6]

### System information

Godot v4.4.1.stable - Windows 11 (build 26100) - Multi-window, 1 monitor - Vulkan (Forward+) - dedicated NVIDIA GeForce RTX 4060 Laptop GPU (NVIDIA; 32.0.15.6607) - AMD Ryzen AI 9 HX 370 w/ Radeon 890M (24 threads)

### Issue description

When deleting an object though `Node.queue_free()` or `SceneTree.queue_delete()`, calling `cancel_free()` on that object in its `NOTIFICATION_PREDELETE` will stop the engine from deleting the object. However, `is_queued_for_deletion()` returns `true` permanently for that object, even though it is not really queued for deletion anymore.

```gdscript
func _ready() -> void:
	var object := ObjectClass.new()
	get_tree().queue_delete(object) # equivalent to Node.queue_free()
	
	await get_tree().create_timer(1.0).timeout
	print("is_queued_for_deletion(): ", object.is_queued_for_deletion()) # true


class ObjectClass extends Object:
	func _notification(what: int) -> void:
		if what == NOTIFICATION_PREDELETE:
			cancel_free()
			print("is_instance_valid(): ", is_instance_valid(self)) # true
			print("is_queued_for_deletion(): ", is_queued_for_deletion()) # true
```

When looking at the source code, this makes sense as `_predelete_ok` [gets set to false](https://github.com/godotengine/godot/blob/4ebf67c12dcdffcb69242569c118a371a654b6ae/core/object/object.cpp#L265), but `_is_queued_for_deletion`, [which is used in `is_queued_for_deletion()`](https://github.com/godotengine/godot/blob/4ebf67c12dcdffcb69242569c118a371a654b6ae/core/object/object.cpp#L2024), remains `true`.

### Steps to reproduce

See code above.
